concerns.text: T005a mandates a hard exit (E_DATASET_MISSING) if external Zenodo/HuggingFace datasets are missing. However, the Plan (Data Availability section) and Spec (Assumptions) explicitly state that no such external datasets exist for N=10-40 and that internal generation is the primary source. This task implements a constraint (FR-009) that, if executed as written, guarantees immediate pipeline failure before any research can occur, violating the constitutional requirement for reproducibility and feasibility.

T016 instructs to 'Calculate NCD using gzip/lzma/bzip2 on the quantized full wavefunction coefficients'. For N=40, a full wavefunction vector (2^40 elements) exceeds the 7GB RAM limit (SC-004) and Constitution Principle VI (sparse only). The Plan explicitly rejects 'Compression on Reduced Representation' as a simpler alternative but then mandates compression on the 'full' vector in the task, creating a physical impossibility that violates the memory constraints and the Plan's own feasibility analysis.

T016 describes generating an 'internal size-matched random baseline' for NCD but fails to specify that this baseline must also be quantized to 16-bit integers (per FR-003a) before compression. NCD requires compressing the concatenation of two quantized strings; compressing a quantized signal against an unquantized baseline (or vice versa) yields invalid NCD results, violating Constitution Principle VII (Algorithmic Information Proxy Validation).

Phase 6 introduces 'MPS bond dimension' as a 'primary algorithmic complexity surrogate' and cites Brown & Susskind. However, the Spec (FR-003, FR-003a) strictly defines the complexity metric as 'lossless compression ratios' only. Introducing a new primary metric without a corresponding Functional Requirement in the spec constitutes scope creep and violates the Single Source of Truth principle, as the spec does not authorize this measurement.

T030 specifies implementing bootstrap resampling with 'a sufficient number of iterations'. The Spec (US-3, FR-006) explicitly defines the acceptance criterion as '1000 iterations'. Using vague language ('sufficient') instead of the explicit number required by the spec risks incomplete implementation and violates the requirement for testable acceptance criteria.
